subject: Multi-session model - D varying among sessions with g0 and sigma cte

messages.author: 5c425464a19143be
messages.subject: Multi-session model - D varying among sessions with g0 and sigma cte
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to fit a multi-session model to estimate density of different bird species in primary and secondary forest. I have data from 6 years - each year is one session - and I would like to obtain density estimates for each year.

Right now I'm able to fit a multi-session model that give only one density estimation:

multimod <- secr.fit(capt.bird, model = list(D~Forest, g0~trapftype, sigma~1), start =c(0.01, 0, -8, 0, 8), mask=formask.bird2, method = "Nelder-Mead")


As I said, this model gives me a single density estimation rather then one for each year, and I get the error message:

1: In model.matrix.default(formula, data = data, contrasts.arg = contrasts) :
  variable 'session' is absent, its contrast will be ignored

but if I check the sessions at the capt.bird object I get:

>factor(session(capt.bird))

[1] capt.bird2011 capt.bird2013 capt.bird2014 capt.bird2015 capt.bird2016 capt.bird2017
Levels: capt.bird2011 capt.bird2013 capt.bird2014 capt.bird2015 capt.bird2016 capt.bird2017

When I try to fit:

multi <- secr.fit(capt.bird, model = list(D~session*Forest, g0~trapftype, sigma~1), start =c(0.01, 0, 0, -8, 0, 8),mask=formask.bird2, method = "Nelder-Mead",
                        details = list(contrasts = list(session = MASS::contr.sdif)))

I get this message:

Error: length(start) == NP is not TRUE
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In model.matrix.default(formula, data = data, contrasts.arg = contrasts) :
  variable 'session' is absent, its contrast will be ignored

The first part I believe has something to do with my starting values (though I've already tried different combinations with no success), but I still get same error message.

capt.bird and formask.bird2 files: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1RWorCcyhHZ0qB3xXJvq_2P_BEECTNTg1

Any help extremely welcome. My apologies if this is a repeated posting, or a basic question.

Thank you!

Bruna Amaral

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multi-session model - D varying among sessions with g0 and sigma cte
parts:
Hello Bruna

I think your data need to be simplified in various ways to become manageable.

1. The mask you provide has been built with a buffer much larger than needed given the apparently small scale of movements - 2000 m would be plenty. The mask can be made much smaller and more manageable by setting keep.poly = FALSE in make.mask (or retrospectively setting to NULL for each mask in the list).

2. You have an enormous number of detectors (what were they? what were the trap types?) and the 'usage' matrix I looked at was very sparse, so I'm suspicious there.

3. You have only a few dozen recaptures overall, so there's probably no need for sophistication in the  detection model. With many (daily?) samples the model will take forever to fit, so I would consider collapsing to one occasion (but I was unsure what was safe because i don't understand the detectors).

4. I haven't seen that 'contrasts' message before - was it really an error or just a warning? It is something I need to check further. However, I think you do not need to be specifying that details option, certainly not until you have everything else sorted.

5. "length(start) == NP is not TRUE" just means your start vector is wrong; it's safer to use the form start = list (D= , g0 =, sigma = ) because then you don't need to provide all beta parameters, not all real parameters if you don't want.

Cheers
Murray

messages.subject: Re: Multi-session model - D varying among sessions with g0 and sigma cte
parts:
Hi Murray,

Thank you very much for your message! here are some more details:

(1) I was using a big mask cause I have different species with different home-range sizes, and some are huge (ant-followers); but I will definitely make it smaller, as you suggested.

(2) Each trap is one 20m long mist-net. We sample for 2 weeks monthly from June to September every year, for 6 years (6 sessions).

In each month we randomly sample in which trails the mist-nets will be (also in the same trails we have lots of tree falls from one month/year to the next), so in each occasion each net is in a slightly different position, so it is treated as a different trap (different GPS coordinates). That's why I have so many traps. I can try to make 'clusters' of nets that are close by and call it one trap, I just don't want to miss any spatial information.

(3) Each occasion is one day of sampling (2 sets of 20-30 nets open from 6am to 12pm). I can also cluster the occasions for the month, rather than one day, so I would have ~5 occasions for each session (each occasion would consist of 15 days of sampling). Would that help in addition to put some of the traps together?

I purposefully choose a species with only a few captures and recaptures to begin my analysis and understand the model, and also to check for errors. I also get the message 'memory exhausted (limit reached?)'  and 'Error: cannot allocate vector of size 911.8 Mb' with the species that I have more data, so I was starting with the ones with fewer captures to have a model running, and later would deal with this memory issue. Probably reducing the number of traps and occasions would help with that, right?

I'm happy to provide an example of a species with more captures and a higher recapture rate if it helps. Files: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1RWorCcyhHZ0qB3xXJvq_2P_BEECTNTg1

(4) You are right, the message I got is not an error, just a warning - I got results, but they are all the same for all the sessions.

Thank you!

Cheers,

Bruna

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multi-session model - D varying among sessions with g0 and sigma cte
parts:
That's interesting, and challenging (verging on impossible) if you want to do one big analysis.  It would be a mistake for me to try and give specific advice. My inclination is (i) break the dataset up into separate analyses, one per year, (ii) collapse occasions within a year, and (iii) aggregate sites with a species-appropriate spatial scale. Treat aggregated detectors as 'count' detectors with appropriate usage (net-days?). Apply some post-hoc or simulation-based checks that aggregation doesn't distort the results.  I wish I could help more.
Murray

parts:
Hi Murray,

One quick question: I did collapsed my occasions for each season together, and I was wondering if I should change the detector type (it was multi) - since now the same animal can be captured in different traps in the same occasion.

I suspect that only the first trap where an individual is captured is being taken into account when I run the model with 'multi' detector. The number of detections is the same individuals captured, and I believe the recaptures are not being used to make the estimates.

Should I try proximity trap?

Thank you!

Cheers,

Bruna

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multi-session model - D varying among sessions with g0 and sigma cte
parts:
Hi
A capthist object with detector type 'multi' and multiple captures of an animal on one occasion should not pass verify(). I would have used something like reduce(CH, by = 'all', outputdetector = 'count') or reduce(CH, by = 'all', outputdetector = 'proximity') to take care of this in one step, although from memory your case is complex so some juggling may be needed. The difference between count and proximity is probably not material, but 'count' requires you to think about binomial vs Poisson counts.
Murray
